Solution.encode.sizes: w is the number of words and L is the encoded length.
Solution.encode.reason: Each iteration can copy the accumulated prefix. Summing w prefix lengths bounded by L gives O(w * L) time. Only a constant number of strings of length up to L are live together.

Solution.decode.sizes: L is the encoded length. Header integers fit within the problem bounds.
Solution.decode.reason: The indices scan each header once and copy each payload once. Returned strings and their list take at most linear space.

Solution.getConcatenation.sizes: n is the length of nums. Space includes the new output list.
Solution.getConcatenation.reason: The allocation holds 2n items and one loop copies both halves.

Solution.groupAnagrams.sizes: w is the number of words, c is the total character count, and the alphabet has 26 letters.
Solution.groupAnagrams.reason: Each character updates a counter once. Counting tuples have constant size, and the groups store w references to input words.

Solution.isAnagram.sizes: n and m are string lengths, and d is the number of distinct characters across both.
Solution.isAnagram.reason: The two scans build frequency dictionaries, and their comparison reads at most d entries. With a fixed alphabet, the space is O(1).

Solution.isValidSudoku.sizes: The problem fixes the board at 9 by 9.
Solution.isValidSudoku.reason: The two loops visit at most 81 cells and track a bounded number of entries in the row, column, and square sets.

Solution.longestCommonPrefix.sizes: w is the number of words and p is the length of the shortest word.
Solution.longestCommonPrefix.reason: zip creates w iterators and yields up to p columns of width w. Each set costs expected O(w). Appending one character at a time can also copy up to p accumulated characters per step.

Solution.longestConsecutive.sizes: n is the length of nums.
Solution.longestConsecutive.reason: Set construction and the outer scan are linear. Each consecutive run is expanded only from its smallest value, so inner scans collectively visit at most n values.

Solution.majorityElement.sizes: n is the length of nums and d is its number of distinct values.
Solution.majorityElement.reason: Each input item updates one map counter and the current maximum. The map stores d counters.

Solution.majorityElement.sizes: n is the length of nums and d is its number of distinct values.
Solution.majorityElement.reason: Counting takes n updates and filtering checks d counters. The map dominates space, and at most two values can exceed n/3.

SolutionBoyerMoore.majorityElement.sizes: n is the length of nums.
SolutionBoyerMoore.majorityElement.reason: The vote pass uses two candidate slots. At most two list.count calls verify candidates, and at most two values are returned.

Solution.maxSubArray.sizes: n is the length of nums.
Solution.maxSubArray.reason: Kadane's loop visits each number once and keeps only the current and best sums.

max_subarray_elements.sizes: n is the length of nums. Space includes the returned slice.
max_subarray_elements.reason: One scan updates sums and boundaries. The final slice copies up to n items.

Solution.maxSubarraySumCircular.sizes: n is the length of nums.
Solution.maxSubarraySumCircular.reason: One pass maintains the total and both Kadane sums in a fixed number of scalar variables.

Solution.productExceptSelf.sizes: n is the length of nums. Space includes the output list.
Solution.productExceptSelf.reason: Prefix and postfix passes each take n steps. Excluding the output, only two running products and indices are needed.

NumMatrix.__init__.sizes: r and c are the row and column counts of the nonempty rectangular input.
NumMatrix.__init__.reason: The constructor delegates to calcPrefixMatrix and retains the resulting table.

NumMatrix.calcPrefixMatrix.sizes: r and c are the row and column counts of the nonempty rectangular input.

NumMatrix.sumRegion.sizes: The prefix table has already been built.

NumArray.__init__.sizes: n is the length of nums.
NumArray.__init__.reason: Each item contributes one cumulative sum to a retained prefix list of length n + 1.

NumArray.sumRange.sizes: The prefix list has already been built.
NumArray.sumRange.reason: Two indexed reads and a subtraction answer the query.

Solution.sortArray.sizes: n is the length of nums and r is max(nums) - min(nums) + 1 for a nonempty input.
Solution.sortArray.reason: The method delegates to counting_sort_with_array. Its count table spans r values and it visits or writes each input element a constant number of times.

Solution.counting_sort_with_hashmap.sizes: n is the length of nums, d is its number of distinct values, and r is its integer range width.
Solution.counting_sort_with_hashmap.reason: Counting and rewriting take n steps each, and the outer reconstruction loop walks all r values. The dictionary holds d counts. Rebuilding the cleared list can temporarily copy a buffer of up to n items.

Solution.counting_sort_with_array.sizes: n is the length of nums and r is its integer range width.
Solution.counting_sort_with_array.reason: The count list has r slots. The inner while loops perform n writes in total because each write consumes one stored occurrence.

Solution.heap_sort.sizes: n is the length of nums. Space includes the new output list.
Solution.heap_sort.reason: Heapify takes linear time. n heap pops each cost at most logarithmic time, and the output accumulates n values.

Solution.sortColors.sizes: n is the length of nums.
Solution.sortColors.reason: Heapify takes linear time, followed by n heap pops. The comprehension holds n values before the slice assignment.

Solution.sortColorsThreePointer.sizes: n is the length of nums.
Solution.sortColorsThreePointer.reason: Each iteration shrinks the unclassified interval by advancing mid or decrementing right. Swaps use constant storage.

Solution.subarraySum.sizes: n is the length of nums.
Solution.subarraySum.reason: Each step computes one prefix sum and performs a fixed number of hash-table operations. At most n + 1 distinct prefixes are retained.

Solution.topKFrequent.sizes: n is the input length and d is the distinct-value count. The prompt guarantees k <= d.
Solution.topKFrequent.reason: Counting takes expected O(n). This implementation sorts the d count/value pairs and then reads up to k results. The map, pairs, and sort workspace use O(d) space.

Solution.twoSum.sizes: n is the length of nums.
Solution.twoSum.reason: The scan does a fixed amount of arithmetic and hash-table work per item. The map stores at most n previously seen values.

Solution.xorQueries.sizes: n is the array length and q is the number of queries. Space includes the returned results.
Solution.xorQueries.reason: One scan builds n + 1 prefix XORs, and each query takes two indexed reads and an XOR.

Solution.characterReplacement.sizes: n is the string length and the problem fixes a 26-character alphabet.
Solution.characterReplacement.reason: The right index advances n times, each with at most one left advance. The map holds at most 26 character counts.

Solution.containsNearbyDuplicate.sizes: n is the input length and k is the nonnegative maximum distance.
Solution.containsNearbyDuplicate.reason: Each right step performs a bounded number of set operations. The maintained window holds at most k + 1 items.

Solution.lengthOfLongestSubstring.sizes: n is the string length and a is the alphabet size.
Solution.lengthOfLongestSubstring.reason: Each right step inserts once, and each left step removes an item at most once across the entire run. The window set contains distinct characters.

Solution.maxProfit.sizes: n is the number of prices.
Solution.maxProfit.reason: Each loop iteration advances the right index once and updates scalar state.

Solution.numOfSubarrays.sizes: n is the length of arr.
Solution.numOfSubarrays.reason: One pass adds each entering value and subtracts at most one leaving value. The window sum and count are scalars.

Solution.evalRPN.sizes: n is the token count. Numeric tokens and intermediate values have the problem's bounded width.
Solution.evalRPN.reason: Each token does constant arithmetic and a bounded number of amortized list operations. Up to n operands can accumulate on the stack.

Solution.generateParenthesis.sizes: n is the number of pairs and C_n is the nth Catalan number. Space includes the returned strings.
Solution.generateParenthesis.reason: Every valid partial prefix extends to an answer, and each answer has at most 2n + 1 prefixes. Each of the C_n leaves joins a length-2n string. The recursion and working stack alone take O(n) space.

Solution.maxSlidingWindow.sizes: n is the input length. The window size k is at most n.
Solution.maxSlidingWindow.reason: Each element is pushed once and popped at most once. Stale entries are removed only when they reach the heap top, so the heap can grow to n entries even for a smaller window.

Solution.mergeTwoLists.sizes: n and m are the two input-list lengths.

MinStack.__init__.reason: The constructor allocates two empty lists.

Solution.checkInclusion.sizes: n and m are the two string lengths, and the alphabet has 26 letters.

Solution.isValidSudoku.sizes: The problem fixes the board at 9 by 9.
Solution.isValidSudoku.reason: Both loops have constant bounds and the tracked sets hold at most a fixed number of entries.

Solution.numRescueBoats.sizes: n is the number of people.
Solution.numRescueBoats.reason: Python's sort dominates the linear two-pointer pass and can use linear temporary workspace.

Solution.fourSum.reason: There are O(n^2) pairs of fixed indices. Each pair gets one O(n) scan because duplicate-skipping loops advance the same pointers. Sorting can use O(n) workspace and results use O(z).

Solution.maxArea.sizes: n is the number of heights.
Solution.maxArea.reason: Each iteration moves one pointer inward, so the interval shrinks at least once per step. The method maintains only a few scalars.

Solution.mergeAlternately.sizes: n and m are the lengths of the input strings.
Solution.mergeAlternately.reason: The alternating scan, tail slices, and final join process O(n + m) characters in total. The list and returned string can each grow to that size.

Solution.merge.sizes: m and n are the counts of valid input elements.
Solution.merge.reason: Each step consumes one input element and writes into an existing slot of nums1.

Solution.removeDuplicates.sizes: n is the length of the sorted input.

Solution.removeDuplicates.sizes: n is the length of the sorted input.
Solution.removeDuplicates.reason: Each value is checked once against the compacted prefix and valid values are written in place.

Solution.reverseString.sizes: n is the number of characters.
Solution.reverseString.reason: Each iteration swaps two existing entries and moves both indices inward.

Solution.rotate.sizes: n is the positive input length.
Solution.rotate.reason: Three in-place reversals collectively touch O(n) entries. The helper is nonrecursive and uses two indices.

Solution.threeSum.sizes: n is the input length and z is the number of returned triplets.
Solution.threeSum.reason: Each of n outer positions starts a linear two-pointer scan. Duplicate skipping advances the same pointer. Sorting can use O(n) workspace and results use O(z).

Solution.trap_bruteforce.sizes: n is the number of heights.
Solution.trap_bruteforce.reason: For each of O(n) positions, the left and right maximum scans together inspect O(n) heights.

Solution.trap_prefix_suffix_sum.sizes: n is the number of heights.

Solution.twoSum.sizes: n is the length of the sorted array.
